speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what caused the power outage at Woodlands Checkpoint on 9 October 2022; (b) whether there are any data breach or losses incurred; and (c) how can such power outages be prevented.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is known regarding the root causes of the power outage at Woodlands Checkpoint on 9 October 2022, including the reasons for the reported failure of the backup power generator measures; and (b) what measures are taken to ensure resilience of Singapore's immigration checkpoints against electrical power failures.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the cause of the failure of the backup power generator at Woodlands Checkpoint on 9 October 2022 despite having been serviced and tested the day before; and (b) what measures, including manual workarounds, does the Ministry have in place to ensure that all border checkpoints are able to continue performing their essential functions, including immigration clearance, in the event of an extended power outage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I invite the Member to seek clarifications today, if need be.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If the Member feels that his questions are addressed today, it may not be necessary for him to proceed with them during the future Sitting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This timing was chosen as it is, typically, an off-peak period at the checkpoint.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The back-up power generator was maintained according to the technical specifications and assessed to be in good working condition during routine weekly and monthly checks, as well as on the day of the scheduled maintenance on 8 October 2022.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: A full load test on the generator had been conducted in August 2022.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the morning of 8 October 2022, it had been subjected to a 30-minute test-run and was working fine.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: While the back-up generator has been in operation since 1999, its usage is low.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is only operated when the building power source is undergoing maintenance or during a power failure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is scheduled for replacement in 2028, according to the specifications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As the hot air re-circulated in the room, the generator engine overheated and shut down.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The condition of the air duct was inspected visually and was assessed to be in good condition in the morning of 8 October 2022.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) system had kicked in, as designed, and provided sufficient time for a proper shutdown of the servers, preventing any data breach or loss.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: ICA has put in additional layers of redundancy to protect our operations from power disruptions.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: There are back-up generators for the main power source.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition, UPS is provided for key systems to ensure operations continuity if the back-up generators fail.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These systems are regularly upgraded during planned maintenance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For an extended power failure which UPS cannot support, ICA has SOPs in place to ensure operations continuity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: This includes activating additional manpower to assist with manual clearance, communicating and advising travellers via multiple channels to avoid non-essential travel and diverting traffic to the other land checkpoint.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These contingency plans were activated during this incident.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We will share the lessons learnt from this incident with stakeholders of other critical infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: First, how was immigration clearance conducted during the power outrage?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Second, why was it necessary to divert traffic to the Tuas Checkpoint?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: ICA implemented the contingency immigration clearance process, which involves the officers taking down the travellers' details and then, performing back-end security screening, creating the travel records using what we have recorded.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As the clearance rate using the contingency process was significantly slower, an operational decision was made to clear vehicles and travellers who were already on the Causeway travelling towards Woodlands Checkpoint or within the Checkpoint; while ICA worked with the Malaysian authorities to divert the inbound vehicles that had yet to enter the Bangunan Sultan Iskandar Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we diverted those who had not entered the CIQ to the Second Link.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: For the outbound vehicles on the Bukit Timah Expressway (BKE) and Woodlands crossings, they were diverted to the Second Link.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We feel that if this was not done, the traffic jam at the Woodlands Checkpoint would have worsened and caused inconvenience to even more travellers.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am sure the individual officers are doing their very best and their work is very much appreciated.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, I would like to ask the Minister of State if there are systemic bottlenecks that ICA can look into to tackle the long waiting times at our land checkpoints.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: One observation by travellers is that, sometimes, not all the immigration counters for vehicles are open.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand, because of limited manpower, ICA dynamically deploys officers to counters in busier zones, leaving counters closed in another zone.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State, then – can ICA prioritise its recruitment and training of more officers so that all car counters are manned to clear travellers in all zones?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And secondly, can ICA increase the number of automated clearance counters for vehicles, especially motorcycles, to relieve some dependence on manned counters?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These are issues that we continuously look at and which we also train our officers for regularly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, while we were preparing for the reopening and easing of travel, these were things we were doing with our officers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I want to assure the Member that we are continuing with this process of continuously looking at how to improve how we handle the situation and how we run the operations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Our officers are very committed to doing this because they understand the needs of the people, especially when they are travelling and especially during the peak periods.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How did ICA ensure that the security of our Woodlands checkpoint was not compromised, that is, that there were no security breaches, such as any illegal or unauthorised entry into Singapore?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, what we did was that during the power outage, our Auxiliary Police Officers (APOs) worked with us and continued to man all critical security posts and access points at Woodlands Checkpoint.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And these critical security posts and access points had the emergency lighting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In addition to that, we also provided APOs portable emergency lamps and they guarded these points.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Also, we had more security patrols throughout the period of the outage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are happy that there were no security breaches.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have Clementi residents who were concerned at the news of what happened during the power outage.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because when a back-up generator is deployed as the main ongoing power supply, it is no longer a back-up system.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because a system may be compromised through many different possibilities and we have to secure our key infrastructure and checkpoints.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Yes, we will have the AAR to be undertaken.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The risks that were highlighted by the Member are things that we look at, as part of our business continuity plan.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In order to do that, agencies work with the critical infrastructure stakeholders and we do have monthly drills that not only look at the issue of power outages.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The works will be carried out in phases because of the complexity of the nature of the works and we also want to carefully plan it, so that we can minimise disruption to ICA's ongoing operations.
